title: Fidelity Degradation Insurance and SLA Pricing Guidance
author: Asha K. Patel
body:
Summary:

This guidance defines an approach for pricing, packaging, and contracting an add-on insurance product that compensates customers when runtime-driven fidelity degradations occur (short-duration quality or capability reductions due to capacity, cost, or preemptible resource constraints). The document explains the insurance product concept, SLA mappings, credit calculations, example pricing bands, recommended commercial wording, implementation milestones, telemetry and audit requirements, and customer-facing communication templates.

Purpose and scope:

- Purpose: Provide a repeatable commercial framework that lets Redwood offer predictable remediation (credits/compensation) to customers for measurable fidelity degradations while protecting platform economics and incentivizing sensible usage patterns.
- Scope: Hosted and Dedicated deployment modes initially; Private deployments considered but require separate legal/KMS/audit controls and are out-of-scope for the 1.0 launch. This guidance covers pricing heuristics, credit mechanics, observability signals, and a rollout roadmap.

Background and rationale:

As customers adopt adaptive fidelity (quantization, model fallbacks, degraded sampling) to manage costs, they request contractual assurances for correctness-sensitive workloads (e.g., legal summarization, billing reconciliation, compliance triage). Traditional uptime SLAs do not capture output quality reductions that are short-lived and controlled by runtime heuristics. The fidelity insurance product is designed to:

1) Translate measurable quality regressions into compensable credit events.
2) Maintain incentives for customers to use adaptive fidelity tools (e.g., fallback variants, cache-first routing).
3) Limit financial open-ended exposure for Redwood via defined caps and tiered pricing.

Key definitions:

- Fidelity Degradation Event (FDE): A measurable, runtime-detected change in model output fidelity for a specific route or customer that is caused by platform-driven routing, fallback, preemption, or quantization changes (not customer prompt changes).
- Fidelity Window: Time-bounded period (default 5 minutes) over which degraded outputs are observed and aggregated for event detection.
- Severity Grade: Classification of FDEs (minor, moderate, major) based on delta in quality metric (BLEU/ROUGE/embedding-similarity/eval-set pass-rate) and customer route importance.
- Insurance Credit: Monetary or usage credit applied to customer account as remediation.

SLA and credit mapping (high-level):

- Minor (severity = minor): Observable 5–10% drop in eval-set pass-rate or >0.85 embedding-similarity delta; credit = 5% of route spend during fidelity window (cap 2x monthly).
- Moderate (severity = moderate): Observable 10–30% drop or embedding-similarity delta >0.70; credit = 15% of route spend during window (cap 5x monthly).
- Major (severity = major): >30% drop or embedding-similarity delta <0.70 for critical routes; credit = 40% of route spend during window (cap 10x monthly).

Note: Route spend = billable tokens/embedding units consumed on the affected route(s) during the fidelity window. These mappings are the baseline and can be tuned during pilot.

Pricing bands and packaging:

We propose three packaging options for customers: Basic, Advanced, and Enterprise. Pricing below assumes a per-month subscription fee + usage band multiplier. All prices are illustrative and require commercial review.

1) Basic (self-serve)
- Monthly fee: $250
- Included coverage cap: up to 2x monthly credits (cumulative).
- Per-incident deductible: $250 equivalent or 2% of monthly spend (whichever higher).
- Suitable for dev/test or low-criticality routes.

2) Advanced (SMB / production)
- Monthly fee: $1,500
- Included coverage cap: up to 5x monthly credits.
- Per-incident deductible: $1,000 or 1.5% of monthly spend.
- SLA: 99.9% fidelity-window monitoring coverage and quarterly joint reviews.

3) Enterprise (custom)
- Monthly fee: custom (starting at $8,000)
- Included coverage cap: negotiable, typical 10x monthly credits with overage caps.
- Deductible: negotiable; typically waived for customers >$100k monthly spend.
- Includes priority remediation, audit trail exports, and per-contract severity thresholds.

Commercial guardrails and caps:

- Maximum annual exposure per customer is capped at min(25% of annual committed spend, $2M) unless explicitly approved by Finance.
- Credits are applied as usage credits first, with cash refunds processed only for exceptional cases and require finance approval.
- Multiple overlapping events within the same fidelity window are de-duplicated and combined into a single incident for crediting.

Observability, telemetry, and detection rules (implementation):

1) Signals required for detection:
- Per-route eval-set pass-rate (rolling window metrics at 1m resolution)
- Embedding similarity baseline and rolling delta per tenant
- Model variant change log (which runtime variant served each request)
- Prefix cache-hit ratio and rate of fallback decisions
- Token-level latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) to correlate load-driven degradations

2) Detection algorithm (prototype outline):
- Maintain a per-route baseline computed over trailing 30d excluding known maintenance windows.
- For each 1m window compute delta = (baseline_pass_rate - current_pass_rate). 
- Apply anomaly suppression for windows with <1000 tokens or <10 eval probes.
- Map delta to severity grade using thresholds defined in SLA mapping.
- Generate FDE incident and attach evidence payload (sampled request ids, variant ids, metric slices).

3) Audit & evidence retention:
- Evidence for credited incidents must be retained for 365 days.
- Provide an exportable incident package (JSON or CSV) to customers under Enterprise.

Contract language (recommended clauses):

1) Fidelity Insurance Addendum (snippet):
"The Provider operates an insurance product that credits Customer accounts for Fidelity Degradation Events attributable to the Provider's runtime decisions. Fidelity Degradation Events are defined in the attached Schedules and are subject to detection rules, deductibles, caps, and exclusions. Credits are applied in accordance with the Provider's published guidance and the customer's selected subscription tier."

2) Exclusions (examples):
- Customer-caused prompt changes or test harnesses.
- Known maintenance windows and scheduled capacity transitions.
- Degradations resulting from third-party model provider outages (unless Redwood controls the model hosting).

Billing mechanics and UI flows:

- Incident generates a provisional credit estimate in Console > Incidents > Fidelity Insurance.
- Customer receives an email notification with a link to the provisional incident package and an appeal window of 7 calendar days.
- If the customer appeals, a Technical Review is kicked off (triage SLA = 5 business days).
- After the appeal window closes or review completes, credit is applied as a usage offset in the next billing cycle.

Implementation roadmap and milestones (90/180/365):

- 0–90 days (Pilot):
  1) Build detection pipeline prototype (per-route baselines, 1m ingest).
  2) Implement provisional incident UI and export package.
  3) Pilot with 3–5 power customers (mixed Hosted/Dedicated).
  4) Validate severity thresholds and credit math against historical incidents.

- 90–180 days (MVP):
  1) Integrate crediting into billing system (usage credits ledger).
  2) Launch Basic and Advanced packaging tiers on Console.
  3) Add audit retention and automated export for Enterprise.
  4) Create sales enablement, legal addendum templates, and partner training.

- 180–365 days (Scale):
  1) Expand to Private deployments (requires legal & security review).
  2) Add predictive pre-notifications for customers approaching deductible thresholds.
  3) Iterate pricing bands based on loss analytics and customer feedback.

Metrics and success criteria:

- Product adoption: % of customers with production routes who purchase insurance within 6 months of availability (target 8% for Advanced tier in year 1).
- False positive rate: proportion of provisional incidents successfully appealed (target <8%).
- Finance impact: annualized credit exposure as % of ARR (target <=1.2% at launch).
- Customer satisfaction: NPS change for customers using the product (target +6 points).

Operational runbook (incident lifecycle):

1) Detection -> Auto-triage (system assigns severity) -> Provisional credit estimate published.
2) Customer notified with evidence packet.
3) Customer may accept or appeal.
4) Technical Review (if appealed): 2 engineers (Platform + Applied-ML) validate evidence and return decision within 5 business days.
4) Billing applies credit; Finance logs the adjustment.

Risks and mitigations:

- Risk: Overcrediting due to noisy detection.
  Mitigation: Conservative thresholds during pilot, appeal window, and human review for Moderate/Major incidents.
- Risk: Adverse selection (customers purchase insurance only for high-risk routes).
  Mitigation: Deductible and pricing bands encourage broad coverage; negotiated enterprise caps.
- Risk: Legal exposure for Private deployments.
  Mitigation: Separate contract track and additional contract controls before availability.

Open decisions (needs leadership/legal/finance signoff):

- Deductible math for high-volume tenants and wholesale exceptions.
- Whether credits are limited to usage offsets or whether cash refunds are permitted as a standard option.
- Final severity thresholds and metric selection (embedding similarity vs. eval pass-rate) for multilingual workloads.

Appendix A — Example detection pseudocode (prototype):

```
# pseudo-python: sliding-window baseline and detection
for route in routes:
    baseline = compute_baseline(route, lookback_days=30)
    for window in windows(route, size=1m):
        if window.tokens < 1000: continue
        pass_rate = eval_probe_pass_rate(route, window)
        delta = baseline.pass_rate - pass_rate
        if delta > grade_thresholds.minor:
            create_fde(route, window, delta)
```

Appendix B — Example console notification copy:

Subject: Provisional Fidelity Insurance Incident for [route-name] (ID: FDE-2029-0810-03)

Hello [Customer Contact],

We detected a temporary fidelity degradation on route [route-name] between 2029-08-10T11:32Z and 2029-08-10T11:37Z. A provisional credit of $1,220 has been calculated and will be applied to your account after the 7-day appeal period unless you request a technical review. View incident details: [link].

Next steps: Accept or request a review within 7 days.

Ownership and next steps:

- Product (owner): lead the pilot, coordinate legal/finance, define tier pricing finalization.
- Applied ML: design and validate detection metrics and thresholds.
- Platform/Serving Runtime: surface variant-level logs, route tagging, and ensure sample retention.
- Finance: implement usage-credit ledger and exposure reporting.
- Legal: prepare addendum templates and finalize exclusions.

This is a restricted, pre-release commercial playbook. For pilot nominations and feedback, contact: asha.patel@redwoodinference.com.
